title: Provider-run telemetry canonical codec
description:
SPIDR slice 2 of 4, cut from task-8e3076177f87458f934a776eca68ba16 after the daemon hard-rejected a 17-file single plan. This is the INTERFACE slice: canonical bytes, digest, and the unreadable-read path.

Hard dependency: task-8e3076177f87458f934a776eca68ba16 (provider-run record contract and closed vocabularies) must be DONE. It supplies the record interface, the closed reason-code/layer arrays including the unreadable-record code, and the aggregate-id derivation. Do not re-declare any of them here.

DELIVERABLE: apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-codec.ts plus its .js bridge and provider-run-codec.test.ts. Mirror apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-codec.ts, which solves exactly this problem for the activation ledger and is the in-repo template.

encodeProviderRunRecord(record) returns {ok:true, bytes, digest, record} or a refusal carrying a stable code and its layer. The decoder verifies BEFORE trusting.

TWO GUARDS, NOT ONE — this is the whole point of the slice. The decode must BOTH recompute the digest over the decoded value AND re-encode and compare bytes. Each guard alone LOOKS sufficient and is not: a digest check alone accepts bytes that decode to an equal value through a different encoding, and a re-encode check alone accepts a consistently-forged pair. A drill that disables one guard must redden a named test; if it does not, the second guard is decorative.

Malformed, truncated and digest-mismatched reads each return the stable unreadable code naming its layer - never a throw, never a partially adopted record.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD — WRITE THE CODEC TESTS FIRST. Create `apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-codec.test.ts`.

DETERMINISM (DoD 1): encoding the same record twice yields BYTE-IDENTICAL output. Compare the BYTES, not the digest — two different byte sequences can be asserted equal through their digests only if the digest function is the thing under test, which is circular.

THE DIGEST DOMAIN (the decision this slice owns): build a record carrying a deliberately WRONG `recordDigest` and assert the encoder OVERWRITES it, producing bytes that verify. If the encoder trusts the incoming value, a caller-supplied digest rides in and every later verification is theatre. Also assert that two records differing ONLY in recordDigest encode to the same bytes — that is what proves the field is excluded from the domain rather than merely overwritten.

ROUND TRIP: encode then decode returns a value equal to the input record, with the digest attached.

FAILURE CASES, each asserting CODE and LAYER and OUTCOME — four layers can refuse in this family, so code alone is one stage away from vacuous:
- Structurally malformed bytes -> PROVIDER_RUN_BYTES_MALFORMED.
- Truncated bytes -> PROVIDER_RUN_BYTES_MALFORMED.
- A digest that does not match its bytes -> PROVIDER_RUN_DIGEST_MISMATCH.
- A recordVersion other than PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_VERSION -> PROVIDER_RUN_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED.
- A record that cannot be read back as a record -> PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_UNREADABLE.
All carry layer PROVIDER_RUN_CODEC. Decode-side refusals carry outcome UNKNOWN (unverifiable evidence confers nothing); encode-side refusals carry REFUSED. Assert the outcome explicitly — it is the field that distinguishes them.

UNDEFINED VS ABSENT VS NULL: JSON.stringify drops undefined, so a record with a field set to undefined and one lacking it can produce identical bytes. Pin whichever behaviour the module chooses; do not leave it unasserted.

These fail until steps 3-4 land.

ENCODE — canonical bytes and the digest (DoD 1). Create `apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-codec.ts`, mirroring activation-ledger-codec.ts.

`encodeProviderRunRecord(record)` returns `{ok: true, bytes, digest, record}` or a `ProviderRunRefusal` from the imported constructors — never a throw, never a partially built value.

THE DIGEST DOMAIN, stated in the module comment because a reader cannot infer it: the digest is computed over the record with `recordDigest` EXCLUDED, then attached. Digesting the whole record would fold the digest field into its own input, which is either circular or silently blesses a stale caller-supplied value. The decoder recomputes over the same reduced domain.

Canonical JSON: sort object keys, recurse arrays in order, and handle the record's nested shapes — frozen objects, `usage`/`usageRefusals` arrays, the nullable `observedStart`/`observedEnd`/`upstreamRefusal`, and the discriminated unions (`ProviderQuantity`, `ProviderText`, `ClaudeDeclaredSelection`) whose `known:false` arms carry code/layer. Decide and DOCUMENT the undefined-vs-absent-vs-null rule; JSON.stringify's silent dropping of undefined is a real collision source.

Validate before encoding: a record failing shape or field checks refuses with PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_MALFORMED or PROVIDER_RUN_FIELD_INVALID at layer PROVIDER_RUN_CODEC, outcome REFUSED.

RE-DECLARE NOTHING — every code, layer, refusal shape and constructor comes from provider-run-refusals.ts, and the record type and version from provider-run-contracts.ts. Keep under 250 lines; if it overruns, split the canonical-JSON helper into its own module rather than trimming validation.

DECODE — BOTH GUARDS (DoD 2, DoD 3), in the same module.

The decoder verifies BEFORE trusting, with two INDEPENDENT guards:
1. Recompute the digest over the decoded value's reduced domain and compare to the digest carried with the bytes.
2. Re-encode the decoded value and compare the resulting BYTES to the input bytes.

Neither is redundant and neither is decorative. A digest check alone accepts bytes that decode to an equal value through a DIFFERENT encoding — key order, spacing, an undefined-vs-absent difference — because the digest is over the value, not the bytes. A re-encode check alone accepts a consistently forged pair where the attacker recomputed the digest to match their own bytes. They stop different attacks, which is why step 6 drills them separately.

Refusal mapping, all at layer PROVIDER_RUN_CODEC with outcome UNKNOWN, since a decode failure is unverifiable evidence rather than a declined operation:
- unparseable or truncated input -> PROVIDER_RUN_BYTES_MALFORMED
- digest mismatch (either guard) -> PROVIDER_RUN_DIGEST_MISMATCH
- recordVersion not PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_VERSION -> PROVIDER_RUN_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED
- decodes but is not a readable record -> PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_UNREADABLE

Never throw, never return a partially adopted record: a caller must not be able to reach a half-populated ProviderRunRecord.

Add the `.js` bridge with bytes exactly `export * from "./provider-run-codec.ts";` plus LF — apps/daemon requires one per production module, and a missing bridge is caught by NEITHER tsc NOR vitest, so it ships silently. Run the step-2 tests; they must now pass.

DRILLS (DoD 2's explicit requirement, plus the digest-domain proof). Capture `sha256sum` of the codec BEFORE each mutation; restore by Edit and verify by `sha256sum` against the captured hash. Never `git checkout` — it reverts to HEAD and would destroy this slice's untracked new files. `git diff` is likewise blind to them, so an empty diff proves nothing.

D1 — DIGEST GUARD ALONE. Disable ONLY the re-encode comparison, leaving digest recomputation. A named test must redden. If none does, the re-encode guard is decorative and DoD 2 is unmet.
D2 — RE-ENCODE GUARD ALONE. Disable ONLY the digest recomputation, leaving the byte comparison. A named test must redden. Drilling both together proves nothing about either, which is why these are separate.
D3 — DIGEST DOMAIN. Make the encoder INCLUDE recordDigest in the digest input. The test asserting that two records differing only in recordDigest encode identically must redden. This is the drill that proves the domain decision is real rather than commentary.
D4 — TRUSTED CALLER DIGEST. Make the encoder keep the caller's recordDigest instead of overwriting it. The wrong-digest test must redden — this is the forged-digest-through-the-front-door path.
D5 — LAYER. Change the layer constant used by the codec's refusals to another member of PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS. A named test must redden ON THE LAYER assertion. If only code assertions redden, the tests are not pinning which of the four stages answered.
D6 — OUTCOME. Flip a decode refusal from UNKNOWN to REFUSED. A named test must redden on the outcome field — epic rail 4 turns on that distinction.

For each drill record the test name and the assertion that reddened, and confirm it reddened on that assertion rather than on a crash.

GATE AND STRUCTURAL CHECKS (DoD 5, DoD 6), each leg's exit code read SEPARATELY — a `&&`-chained run reports one status for two legs and a piped run reports the pipe's tail:
1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck; echo "TYPECHECK_EXIT=$?"`
2. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; echo "TEST_EXIT=$?"`
Both must print 0. Record the vitest summary line and confirm a NONZERO executed test count — a run matching no files also exits 0.

DoD 4, mechanically checkable: `grep -n 'PROVIDER_RUN_' apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-codec.ts` must show every code and layer arriving via IMPORT, with zero local re-definitions. Any bare string literal matching a member of PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_CODES or PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS is a duplicate of the authority slice 1 owns.

Also confirm the codec selects only the SIX codes that belong to this stage — RECORD_MALFORMED, FIELD_INVALID, VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, BYTES_MALFORMED, DIGEST_MISMATCH, RECORD_UNREADABLE. Selecting REPLAY_DIVERGED, EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT or a store code would put the codec's verdict in the ledger's vocabulary.

Structural:
- `provider-run-codec.js` exists with bytes exactly `export * from "./provider-run-codec.ts";` plus LF. Compare against the two sibling bridges rather than eyeballing, and confirm LF not CRLF.
- `grep -c ''` provider-run-codec.ts: under 250.
- `apps/daemon/src/index.ts` unchanged — index-surface.test.ts:267 pins EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length to 61.
- Slice 1's files unchanged: `git status --porcelain apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-contracts.* apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-refusals.*` must show nothing from this task.

FOREIGN RED: shared worktree, and slice 1's worker may still be finishing. Apply the path-attributed-baseline rail; the delta intersected with provider-run-codec.* must be EMPTY. Disclose foreign red verbatim, never repair it.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, COMMIT, HANDOFF. Invoke the adversarial-self-review skill, then work this checklist — each item is how THIS slice fails while looking finished:

1. Is `recordDigest` excluded from its own digest input? If not, the codec digests its own digest field and can bless a caller-supplied value. Re-read the domain and confirm D3 and D4 both reddened.
2. Are the two decode guards genuinely independent? If disabling either one alone leaves the suite green, that guard is decorative and DoD 2 is unmet regardless of how green the run is.
3. Does every failure assertion pin code AND layer AND outcome? Four stages can refuse in this family and the refusals module says a code-only test goes vacuous the moment another stage answers first.
4. Was any code, layer or refusal shape re-declared locally instead of imported from provider-run-refusals.ts?
5. Did the codec select a code belonging to the composition, ledger or reader stage?
6. Can any input reach a partially adopted ProviderRunRecord, or cause a throw instead of a refusal?
7. Is the undefined-vs-absent-vs-null rule DOCUMENTED and tested, not merely whatever JSON.stringify happened to do?
8. Any probe, scratch or generated evidence file left behind? Epic rail 5.

COMMIT BY EXPLICIT PATHSPEC naming only the three `provider-run-codec.*` paths. Never `git add -A` (epic rail 3). If a foreign whole-tree commit already swept your bytes in, do NOT amend, reset or re-commit — hand QA the base-ref diff over the owned paths.

HANDOFF (Clause 1): this slice lands a pure surface with no runtime caller yet, which is permitted only by naming the task that will compose it — task-1a7ff170ee544a3a8a10962c25e2ca5b (durable ledger), with task-ea27beb6e1954d0e9dba8ad49cc1641e (normalize) as the remaining sibling. THE SLICE-1 WORKER SPLIT THE VOCABULARY, which changes what this slice imports. My original task description assumed one contract module. There are TWO: provider-run-contracts.ts holds the record, the store port and the aggregate derivation; provider-run-refusals.ts holds PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_CODES, PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_LAYERS, the ProviderRunRefusal shape and the two constructors. That split was explicitly permitted by slice 1's plan ("if it overruns, split the vocabularies into their own module") and it is the right shape. Import codes and layers from the REFUSALS module, not from contracts.

THE DIGEST DOMAIN IS THE REAL DESIGN DECISION HERE, and it is not in the DoD. `recordDigest: string` is a FIELD ON ProviderRunRecord (contracts.ts:145). A digest computed over the whole record therefore includes the digest field itself, which is either circular or, worse, quietly digests a STALE value carried in from a caller — and then verifies successfully against bytes nobody can independently reproduce. The domain must be the record MINUS recordDigest, computed and then attached, and the decoder must recompute over the same reduced domain. This must be pinned by a test that constructs a record carrying a WRONG recordDigest and shows the encoder overwrites rather than trusts it; otherwise a forged digest rides in through the front door.

ENCODE REFUSES, DECODE ANSWERS UNKNOWN. The refusal module states the rule ("Reader refusals are always UNKNOWN: unverifiable evidence confers nothing") and provides both constructors. Encoding a malformed record is an operation being DECLINED (`providerRunRefusal("REFUSED", ...)`); failing to read durable bytes is unverifiable evidence (`providerRunUnknown(...)`). Getting this backwards would let unreadable durable bytes present as a mere declined operation, which epic rail 4 forbids. The outcome field must be asserted alongside code and layer.

WHAT THIS SLICE IMPORTS — FROM provider-run-refusals.ts, not contracts:

THE DIGEST DOMAIN IS THE DEFECT THIS SLICE MOST LIKELY SHIPS. `recordDigest` lives ON the record. A codec that digests the whole record digests its own digest field, and the failure is not a crash — it is a codec that happily verifies bytes whose digest was supplied by the caller. Compute over the record MINUS recordDigest, attach afterwards, and recompute over the same reduced domain on the way back. Prove it with a record carrying a deliberately WRONG recordDigest: the encoder must overwrite it, and the resulting bytes must verify. If the encoder trusts the incoming value, a forged digest rides in through the front door and every later verification is theatre.

TWO GUARDS, EACH INDEPENDENTLY DRILLED. Digest recomputation alone accepts bytes that decode to an equal value through a different encoding; re-encode comparison alone accepts a consistently forged pair. They fail on different attacks, so drilling them together proves nothing about either — disable exactly one at a time and require a named test to redden for each.

CANONICAL MEANS DETERMINISTIC ACROSS SHAPES, not just sorted keys. The record nests frozen objects, arrays (`usage`, `usageRefusals`), nullable fields (`observedStart`, `observedEnd`, `upstreamRefusal`) and discriminated unions (`ProviderQuantity`, `ProviderText`, `ClaudeDeclaredSelection`). An `undefined` property and an ABSENT property must not encode the same way as an explicit `null` unless that is a stated decision — JSON.stringify silently drops undefined, so a record with a field set to undefined and one without the field produce identical bytes and therefore identical digests. Decide it, state it in the module comment, and test it.

FOUR LAYERS CAN REFUSE IN THIS FAMILY, and the refusals module says so explicitly. Every test must assert code AND layer AND outcome. A test asserting only the code stays green the moment the composition or ledger stage starts answering first — the exact failure the vocabulary's own header warns about.

DO NOT RE-DECLARE ANYTHING. Every code, layer, refusal shape and constructor is imported. If you type a string literal that already appears in PROVIDER_RUN_LEDGER_CODES, you have duplicated the authority this four-slice split exists to keep single. DoD 4 makes this checkable by grep.

DO NOT SELECT ANOTHER STAGE'S CODE. Seventeen codes exist; only six belong to this slice. PROVIDER_RUN_REPLAY_DIVERGED, PROVIDER_RUN_EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT and the store codes are the ledger's, and answering with one here would put the codec's verdict in the ledger's vocabulary.
